subject: Commit floor split negotiation — GPU floorplan arbitration with EmergentAI
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <anguyen@emergentai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@emergentai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit floor split negotiation — GPU floorplan arbitration with EmergentAI

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning, team. Quick recap from our side and two asks before legal takes the redline: 

1) We like the principle of a base "floor" of dedicated GPUs for steady-state inference (predictable latency), plus a burst pool for episodic spikes during training/ingestion.
2) The sticking point is how the floor is measured across zones and whether burst consumption can preempt floor capacity during short spikes.

Can Redwood do the following in the contract: define the floor as a per-region committed minimum (so we have SLA coverage in our primary region), and allow burst to consume additional spare capacity but not to reduce the floor SLA during a 15-minute window? If that window is breached more than 3 times/month, we need an automatic escalation path to either (a) provision an interim top-up at pro-rated cost or (b) credit back the difference.

Also attaching our utilization snapshot — Q2 shows steady 55% 95th-percentile GPU utilization with three clear spike days in June. We want the deal math to reflect that pattern (not the Q1 training-heavy month).

Attachments: utilization_snapshot_q2.pdf

--
Alex Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure, EmergentAI
anguyen@emergentai.com

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <anguyen@emergentai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Priya Shah <priya@emergentai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit floor split negotiation — GPU floorplan arbitration with EmergentAI

Alex — thanks, good notes and appreciated the Q2 file. High level response and proposal below.

Proposal summary (contract language we can include):
- Floor definition: committed baseline is specified as "region-primary floor" (e.g., 120 vGPU-equivalents in us-west-2). That baseline is SLA-backed (99.9% availability measured at regional routing layer).
- Burst policy: Burst can use available capacity in the same region but is explicitly best-effort and annotated as non-SLA; burst consumption will not be allowed to reduce the floor allocation for the duration of any 15-minute interval monitored by our telemetry.
- Breach remediation: If floor availability drops below the committed baseline for more than 15 continuous minutes, and this occurs >3 times in a 30-day window, Redwood will (customer choice) either (a) provision a temporary tranche at pro-rated rate or (b) issue a service credit equal to pro-rata floor downtime.

Operational notes: to make the monitoring robust we will wire up a dedicated metric (region.floor.available) that will feed into the Console dashboards and alerting. That will let both teams validate incidents before invoking remedies.

Next steps I recommend:
- Ben and I will draft short contract language for the SLA + breach remediation clause (two paragraphs) and circulate by end of day tomorrow.
- Marissa will produce a 6-month staggered floor plan aligning with Q2 utilization trends — proposing a 10% headroom buffer for month-to-month variance.
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether you want the temporary tranche option or credits as the default remediation.

Attachments: proposed_floorplan_v3.xlsx (contains month-by-month vGPU counts and assumed burst pool thresholds).

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alex Nguyen <anguyen@emergentai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Priya Shah <priya@emergentai.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit floor split negotiation — GPU floorplan arbitration with EmergentAI

Chiming in with the deal-side perspective and a pricing note.

- We can hold region-floor SLAs as Soojin described. The temporary tranche (option a) will be charged at a short-term top-up rate equal to 1.6x the committed monthly unit price (covers capacity reservation overhead). Credits (option b) will be capped at 20% of that month’s committed cost to avoid negative incentives.
- For EmergentAI’s Q2 pattern (55% median, 3 spike days), my rough recommend: commit to a floor equal to 140 vGPU-equivalents (about 10% above 95th steady) with a 200 vGPU burst pool available regionally. That reduces chance of invocation while keeping your unit economics reasonable.

Operationally we should also add an observability SLA: shared dashboard access + weekly 15-minute sync for 4 weeks post-activation to validate telemetry and ensure proper routing.

If EmergentAI prefers credits over temporary tranches, we can re-run the economics in the spreadsheet; credits push more risk to Redwood and will slightly increase committed-floor pricing.

Next: I’ll add the pricing rows into proposed_floorplan_v3.xlsx and turn it into an appendix for the term sheet by EOD.

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Priya Shah <priya@emergentai.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Nguyen <anguyen@emergentai.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commit floor split negotiation — GPU floorplan arbitration with EmergentAI

Soojin, Ben — thanks, this is exactly the direction we wanted. Two quick clarifications from procurement/legal: 

1) Can the breach remediation trigger be measured at the cluster level instead of just a regional aggregate? We operate a multi-cluster setup and need to ensure one noisy cluster doesn't throttle another.
2) On pricing: procurement prefers the credit path (option b) because it gives us more predictability from a cash-flow standpoint. If credits increase committed-floor pricing, please show both variants in the appendix.

We are ok with the 10% headroom recommendation as long as the appendix shows monthly pro-rating for growth months (we expect +8% month-over-month for two months after onboarding).

If you can get a revised term sheet with both remediation pricing options and a short paragraph about cluster-level monitoring by EOD Friday we can push to legal next week.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Shah
Director of Procurement, EmergentAI
priya@emergentai.com
